prompt.context: Your client is a global consumer packaged goods company — Grime Co. Grime Co. makes paper products (like paper towels), home cleaning products, and laundry care products. The company's Board of Directors has set an aggressive net sales target of $2 billion by 2015 (four years). Currently, net sales are at $1 billion. The CEO has come to you to ask for help. Note: Net sales = Retail sales minus trade spend. Trade spend is what manufacturers pay distributors or retailers to incentivize them to sell their products to end consumers.
prompt.question: Evaluate Grime Co.'s position and help develop a strategy to deliver top-line net sales of $2 billion by 2015.

clarifying_info.q: Which growth strategies has Grime Co. already considered?
clarifying_info.a: We would like you to brainstorm the options first.

clarifying_info.q: How are sales divided across categories?
clarifying_info.a: Sales are divided evenly — 33% each — across paper products, home cleaning products, and laundry care products.

clarifying_info.q: How much cash does Grime Co. have available for investment?
clarifying_info.a: The company has low profit margins and does not want to take on additional debt, so cash available for investment is about $300 million.

clarifying_info.q: Does Grime Co. have any other constraints or priorities?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — the company has a strong stance on sustainability.

clarifying_info.q: How much will market growth contribute to the 2015 target?
clarifying_info.a: Market growth alone will bring sales to $1.5 billion by 2015. The company is growing overall at 10% and expects to maintain constant market share (10% compounded over four years is roughly $500 million incremental). Growth is about the same across all three categories.

clarifying_info.q: Does Grime Co. have any new products in development?
clarifying_info.a: Yes. There is a new toilet cleaning product near launch. Price will be $5 per unit, but requires 20% trade spend per product to reach volume targets. It is expected to sell 40 million units on average per year. No additional investment is required — it is a sunk cost.

clarifying_info.q: Has Corporate Development identified any acquisition targets?
clarifying_info.a: Yes — two high-priority targets: Organoclean and Home Defense Inc.

clarifying_info.q: Can Grime Co. buy both targets?
clarifying_info.a: No — given the $300 million budget, a quick 1.5x sales multiple suggests Grime Co. can only buy one.

exhibits.title: New Product Calculations
exhibits.shows: A step-by-step calculation table for the new toilet cleaning product, showing current net sales, projected 2015 net sales from market growth, the deficit, and the key product economics inputs (price, trade spend, average annual units).

exhibits.title: Acquisition Calculations: Sales Forecast
exhibits.shows: A comparison table of two acquisition targets — Organoclean and Home Defense Inc. — showing their product focus, current sales, annual growth rate, and year-by-year projected sales through 2015.

exhibits.title: Acquisition Calculations: Synergy Considerations
exhibits.shows: A framework listing potential positive and negative synergies for each acquisition target, along with a financial summary of how synergies affect the path to the $2 billion 2015 target for each option.

framework: Market growth: Growth through maintaining market share in a growing market

Organic growth: Internal actions to drive revenue — e.g., price adjustments, advertising, new geographies, vertical integration, promotions, better placement, new products (interviewer steers candidate to new products as the only viable organic lever)
Inorganic growth: Growth through acquisition or joint venture

questions.prompt: How much net sales growth will market growth alone deliver by 2015, and what is the remaining deficit?
questions.guidance: Market growth at 10% CAGR compounded over 4 years on a $1B base delivers ~$500M incremental, reaching $1.5B. The deficit to the $2B target is $500M. Candidate does not need to calculate; just confirm the figure if asked.

math.answer: $500 million deficit remaining after market growth

questions.prompt: How much net sales will the new toilet cleaning product contribute per year?
questions.guidance: Calculate net selling price after trade spend, then multiply by units. Net price = $5 × (1 − 20%) = $4. Annual net sales = $4 × 40M units = $160M. New deficit = $500M − $160M = $340M.

steps: Annual net sales = $4 × 40 million units = $160 million
math.answer: $160 million per year; remaining deficit = $340 million

questions.prompt: Based on the sales forecast alone (ignoring synergies), which acquisition target should Grime Co. buy to close the $340M deficit?
questions.guidance: Organoclean: $150M × (1.10)^4 ≈ $220M. Home Defense Inc.: $200M × (1.20)^4 ≈ $410M. Instruct candidate to round to nearest $10M. Since Grime Co. can only buy one (budget ~$300M at 1.5x sales multiple), Home Defense at $410M projected 2015 sales appears to close the $340M gap, but Organoclean at $220M does not. However, the candidate must also evaluate synergies before concluding.

steps: Budget check: at 1.5× sales, Organoclean ≈ $225M (within $300M); Home Defense ≈ $300M (at limit — can only buy one)

questions.prompt: What positive and negative synergies should be considered for each target, and how do they affect the financials?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm distribution, procurement, manufacturing, back-office, co-branding, and scale synergies (positive) as well as cultural mismatch, antitrust, values clash, and brand dilution (negative). Key quantitative synergies to land on: (1) Grime Co. can leverage its Europe distribution network — $40M year-one additional sales, expected to triple to $120M by 2015, applicable to both targets. (2) Home Defense's bug killers (25% of its sales) use harmful chemicals that Grime Co. will not sell and cannot reformulate — those products must be discontinued, reducing Home Defense's 2015 sales by $102.5M ($410M × 25%). Final math for each path must be compared to the $500M deficit.

math.setup: Organoclean path: $500M deficit − $160M new product − $220M Organoclean 2015 − $120M Europe synergy = ? | Home Defense path: $500M deficit − $160M new product − ($410M − $102.5M) Home Defense net − $120M Europe synergy = ?
steps: Home Defense: discontinued sales = $410M × 25% = $102.5M; net 2015 sales = $410M − $102.5M = $307.5M
Home Defense path: $500M − $160M − $307.5M − $120M = −$87.5M (overshoots target, but sustainability constraint rules out the target anyway)
Sustainability constraint: Home Defense's core bug-killer products conflict with Grime Co.'s values — making Organoclean the only viable choice
math.answer: Organoclean path closes exactly to $0 deficit; Home Defense path fails sustainability screen

brainstorming.prompt: What organic growth strategies could Grime Co. pursue to close the gap?

categories.name: Pricing
ideas: Price adjustments (up or down) to drive volume

categories.name: Products
ideas: Launch new products (only viable organic lever for this client)

recommendation: Grime Co. should pursue a three-pronged growth strategy: (1) capture organic market growth (~$500M), (2) launch the new toilet cleaning product (~$160M net sales/year), and (3) acquire Organoclean (~$220M in 2015 sales plus ~$120M from Europe distribution synergies). Together these paths reach the $2 billion net sales target by 2015.

Of the two acquisition targets, we recommend Organoclean. Although Home Defense Inc. shows faster top-line growth, its bug-killer products conflict with Grime Co.'s sustainability values and would have to be discontinued, eroding projected sales. Organoclean aligns with Grime Co.'s mission and, with the Europe distribution synergy, closes the gap to zero.
risks: Growth trajectory of Organoclean could change
Purchase price could exceed Grime Co.'s $300M budget
Organoclean could be unprofitable — analysis was sales-focused only
Using all available cash limits other investments
Doubling in size could stretch the organization — too fast

Conduct detailed DCF valuation and determine BATNA

Compare acquisition NPV against other potential uses of capital
Roll out new toilet cleaning product
Update systems and organization to support growth
